item.title: Dark Dogs Ritual
item.description: A Dark Dog that is being summoned by a group of stray dogs and chases after them to feed.
item.content:encoded:
Greenlight: yes

Page layout: SCP article

Elevator pitch: Stray dogs goes into a forest to commence a ritual involving a black dog with the unidentifiable breed to have it fed. It only comes once three weeks; when that happens, the Dark dog will choose which dog to eat based on its bravery (fending off the creature). It will attack humans, will kill them but will not eat them.

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

Central Narrative: Dr Fox observes them afore and tries to understand why these dogs are circling one particular spot, first time watching the dogs the research team had no idea about the three-week circle. So when the last day of the third week hits a giant dog appears and begin to chase the dogs around trying to find one that is stronger, because all of the dogs dispersed its attacked spot where the researcher was and started to hunt them down. Dr Fox attempted to fend off the creature but was dragged under a car by three other dogs. Same with another researcher (they all hide) They hid under the car for 7 hours while the creature continues to hunt after dogs until it found one that began to bark at it, it ate the dog and disappeared back to the forest.

Later, Dr Fox wants to learn why one specific spot, so they dig the area and founds skeletons of a man (named Damian) and a dog. Knowing this, they investigate the whole forest and learns that the bodies were, murder victims. After extensive investigation, the lead points to his roommate. It said that Damian left his dorm to take a walk in the morning with his dog on 01/01/2014 and never came back. The roommate ends up being the one that killed Damian and the dog. While in containment, the stray dogs started to circle the site and caused containment breach, and the dark dog bites off Dr Fox’s hand (severely injuring her). And she learns that the dog and Damian’s skeletons when together were the ones that were manifesting the dark dog.

Hook/Attention: basically a little jab on idea that dogs can sense evil spirits.

item.title: cartoon TV
item.description: A TV which creates cartoon logic and replace your brain pattern by a cartoon character.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article

SCP XXX is a cathode-ray tube TV which creates a field around it. In the field, everything is acting as if it exists in a cartoon. For example, you can´t fall down as long as you don´t look down.

The other anomalous property is that everyone observing a cartoon character in the TV has their brain pattern completely overlapped by the exactly cartoon character that was observed. For example, if you look at a cartoon dinosaur who is sentient, then you will believe you are a cartoon dinosaur.

Origin story: The object was recovered after a raid on the abandoned shopping mall of ████████, what seemed like a Chaos insurgency hideout, turned out to be a place to brainwash people with the help of the TV and a cartoon of chaos insurgency soldiers , into the believe that they are chaos insurgency soldier.

item.title: SCP idea: greg the normal guy
item.description: A normal guy who is so normal it's an anomoly
item.content:encoded:
Greg is a 23 year old white man who is described by those who interacted with him as unremarkable and boring in every way. He is noted as having an aura of normalcy that temporarily makes people around him as boring as he is, as well as seemingly nullifying any anomolies until they have left an area of 10 feet around him
On humans, the effects can last anywhere from 2 hours after they've left or even a full week.

I'd love some feedback and ideas for this article

item.title: New SCiP: Just A Very Common Spectroscope (awaiting greenlights)
item.description: Which can turn also common light into deadly radiations
item.content:encoded:
Which can turn also common light into deadly radiations and then wreck the universe

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Sci-fi

Elevator Pitch: An optical widget which can mutate the wave length of electromagnetic waves it is exposed to nearby.

Central Narrative: Beyond some experiment logs, The real escalation starts shortly after the obtaining of the object by the Foundation. As the energy carried by light will magnify with the shortening of wave length, energy coming from nowhere accumulates in the universe and finally caused… deviation of balance of material and energy. Then unexpected results, like the worst - affect the gradual cosmic expansion or bring near the final collapse.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • What will happen if common, visible light around you turn into UV radiation, radioactive X- or even Gamma rays that will kill you in minutes?
  • We all seem indifferent to ectoentropic anomalies now since we've already had enough of them, but few have considered what consequential, long-term impact that "generating infinite water/favorite pizzas/inks/… from void" will do to a coherent universe. But they repaid now.

Additional Notes:

  • I'm not sure a spectroscope can work as the thing. Not having any expertise in optics, so I Googled and found an effect called "frequency doubling" similar to this. But as I know all these obeys the law of energy conservation (idk the actual mechanism). What better title can be applied other than "The Spectroscope" if so?
  • Not very sure how to merge the final world-threatening narrative into this ordinary object-describing document. Will a research report (regarding the status of the universe) or a test log work well?

Sincere thanks from an unexperienced writer! This idea has been around me for quite a while. After some nearly-failed trials of longer skips I wanna switch to an easier one…


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch

Anomalous-D (AD) is an extradimensional parasite which feeds on the pain, fear, grief or rage of other sentient entities. It became entangled with our reality and assumed human form eventually finding its way into a Foundation D Class assignment after being captured and convicted of a string of sadistic crimes against animals and people. Its position as a D Class brings it into frequent close proximity of various other anomalies. Anomalous D devises novel ways provoke or torture these anomalies undetected so that it can feed off their pain and rage.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

  • Containment procedure
  • Description of Entity
  • Description of how the creature came to be in containment / details of anomalous nature
  • Addenda:
    • Incident report: Containment breach first drawing scrutiny of AD
    • Memo: List of incident reports possibly involving AD
    • Interview: Log of the interview which reveals AD’s status as anomalous.
    • Interview: Log of feeding procedure
    • Memo: Detailing the variability of AD’s appearance
    • Memo: Possible reclassification as Keter / Thaumiel

Hook / Attention Grabber:

Following a major incident, the Foundation has confined it but is not sure that it is completely contained. Still, the possibility that this new anomaly may be used to injure or possibly destroy other anomalies is cannot be ignored.

Additional Notes:

Anomalous D typically resides between dimensions and might encounter various manifestations of other trans-dimensional creatures on its travels. It would not normally be able to feed on these entities as they would either be too powerful or impossible to hold on to. But in this reality it has found itself – quite accidentally – in a situation where the SCP foundation has trapped them and rendered them unable to defend themselves. Its motivation is to feed on their stress while not getting snared itself.

I expect that I’ll need lots of discussion and refinement to get this where I want it to be. This would be my first SCP contribution and I’m not an experienced writer. Additionally, most of what interests me in this concept are its possibilities for world-building and future story-telling. It will be challenging to bring this to life in a way that hooks the reader while also pointing to the other possibilities.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Self-Casting Spell
item.description: An article about the people made out of thaumaturgy, who are also kinda Polish. For more, see inside.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A thaumaturgical sentient life-form, living deep in syberia, their culture with strong Polish influences left by Sybiraks. (Sybiraks were the Polish people resettled to Syberia.) It explores both the effects of Polish diaspora and the foundation containing a society.

Central Narrative: It starts off with the special containment procedures (the fenced off part of syberia), then there is a description (about how their bodies are made of what is basically sigils, about how they exchange spells that modify them as plasmids). Then it describes their culture, and the addeneum, where it is described how the sybiraks discover them and describe them, and offer them vodka and rabbit's blood, and how their societies get together, learning from each other and “forming a symbiosis”. It ends with the Incident, when they almost had a civil war.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The concept, I think. Also the ala genetics that arise inside them, and the weird stuff that arises cause of sentient beings being able to trade plasmids.

Additional Notes: Catholic sentient spells, which form tribes. An idea so weird, that it can work. Also their tribe is divided into three groups:
The Ultracatholics, lead by a Fanatical Pariah Priest, who want to make the other groups just as catholic.
The Tolerant, lead by the youngest of the elders, who want to cooperate with The Foundation, and to learn more of the outside world
The Traditionalists, lead by their shaman, who want to be freed and allowed to go back to the old Yakut ways.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] - SCP Article
item.description: Idea for a humanoid SCP that suffers from some form of mental illness with world-ending properties.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Tragedy

Page Type: This is my first SCP, the page layout/type will be simple with the standard containment and description with possible addendums.

Elevator Pitch: Although additional details may be added to the SCP, the core story being told is that this SCP is severely depressed and suicidal but is also theoretically capable of destroying the world via some form of anomalous powers that allows it to alter or change either the space-time continuum, quantum mechanics, or the foundations of existence, with more focus on the SCP's own mental health and how the Foundation can help the entity but obviously not in an altruistic way.

+ block
- Title for hiding text

Central Narrative: Containment procedures will first introduce the situation the SCP is in, introducing two Foundation Personnel that are sent by the ethics committee to be constant check-ups on the SCP, with the SCP being more beneficial being in home confinement accompanied by weekly therapy sessions. Footnotes and Addendums will include 'non-essential' information on the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP is an extraordinarily powerful entity, quickly displaying its power to being able to stop a category-5 cyclone off the coast of Koror City, Palau before quickly dropping off the grid only to be found two days later on the island of Lesbos, Greece. Displaying a unique power that will slowly unveil itself through the course of the article as being able to change or alter a quintessential to the existence of creation, example if the entity so desired it could imagine the Foundation as to never existing or even go so far as to do it to all of existence yet do to the properties it would be classified as Keter if it weren't for the entity's own cooperation it has the classification of Safe as it has no desires to flee containment although refuses to leave its home to a more secure site.

Additional Notes: The focus of the article is less on the anomalous properties but more on how the Foundation interacts with an entity of uttermost world-ending power who suffers from depression and suicidal tendencies, showing the Foundation a more empathic side even if it isn't in an altruistic light.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.description: A seemingly insignificant script which mysteriously appears
item.content:encoded:
A seemingly insignificant script which mysteriously appears in popular online multiplayers, generates a user account of which in game exposure can influence the mind.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: The SCP would be a few lines of code, which would transfer itself from one online multiplayer game to another.

Once the script is embedded within its host, it becomes uneditable or deletable, generating a fictitious user account, referred to as SCP-XXXX-1 (however the script contains not enough code to emulate a user account, leaving foundation staff puzzled).

SCP-XXXX-1 is always generated with an identical username (making identifying affected games an easier task). SCP-XXXX-1 spends a majority of its time in its "inactive" state. However, during short periodic "active" states it performs in game tasks, including text or voice communication (important to monitor for potential interviews and testing).

Any player (in game) to interact or be exposed to SCP-XXXX-1 would start developing symptoms of online addiction, anti-social behaviours and dysphoria.

Central Narrative: This article will be written according to the standard layout. Starting with containment procedures, a description and finishing with an addendum.

containment procedures will outline only monetization instructions for the host game ( including a cover-up story for participating publishing companies to grant the SCP foundation moderation privileges in addition to the games code). Players coming into "contact" with SCP-XXXX-1 are automatically added to foundation listings for interviews and eventual administration of amnestics. Because of its shifting nature, it is considered "not contained". However, due to SCP-XXXX-1's docile and collaborative personality, it has been classed as Euclid.

The description will detail the SCP's nature, it's odd properties and theories. In addition to, SCP-XXXX-1's description, behavioural patterns and anomalous effects on players and how to recover from the latter. Finally, ending with the story of the SCP's discovery

The addendum will feature a list of games the SCP was previously part of.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article seeks to create a fictitious origin for online additions to MMOs and becoming anti-social. In addition, this article is inspired by the collective input of the ChilloutVR community, by an inside joke/meme (hence "Joke SCP") of this very SCP joked to be the source of users who spend their lives in virtual reality (and by extension any other online multiplayers)

Additional Notes: I have a few concerns about copyright. Due to the nature of this article, it will rely heavily on existing games and companies to create the narrative. Am I allowed to use the names of existing companies?

item.title: The Lightswitch (Rewrite, seeking Greenlight)
item.description: An SCP is lost under questionable circumstances. [thread locked, repeat]
item.content:encoded:
An SCP is lost under questionable circumstances. An investigation begins to reveal lies within the Foundation.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): Brief SCP article warning not to look into it (some sort of memetic hazard), most of the content being behind a high clearance level Addendum.

Elevator Pitch: A body-stealing lightswitch is handed around between various GOI’s that allows someone to forcibly take control of another.

Central Narrative: Created by a failed anartist, the UIU collected it from an anomalous smuggler trying to pawn over various low-level anomalies for a quick buck. The smuggler mysteriously vanished, and the UIU soon discovered it had the ability to allow people to enter the bodies of others (essentially controlling them and allowing access to their memories), and almost immediately it became a high priority target from the Foundation and other GOI’s.

+ show block
– hide block

After a series of raids, exchanges, purchases and various under-the-table dealings it finally lands in the Foundation's hands. It gets stolen once more (all too easily, its theft generates a lot of discontent with the Site Manager/containment directors complaining of higher up meddling), but the Foundation’s upper brass immediately demand they cease all investigation/pursuit attempts on it.

Soon after, the Foundation begins launching a series of extremely successful raids on other GOI’s, all ordered from the top brass only (with little communication to various MTF commanders/field directors). This isn’t unheard of (espionage naturally being confidential), but it does begin to grow concern of the lack of communication. A low level Researcher, Dr. Jonathan Moyer, looks more into the situation.

He starts pulling back layers and layers of lies, revealing that all the times the SCP hopped from GOI to GOI it was meticulously logged by the Foundation. He discovers that the UIU never actually discovered it, rather it was left on their doorstep one day. Turns out, the anartist who created it never existed, and at this point Dr. Moyer is closing in on the truth; all signs are pointing at the Foundation’s upper brass having far more influence than previously thought. As he starts following this trail to its end, he is suddenly killed during a containment breach of a seperate SCP he was working with. The top brass claim the breach was sabotage by the Chaos Insurgency, and refuse to allow anyone to look into it.

After this, the containment procedures are appended to include a (false) addendum mentioning an anti-memetic hazard, or some other nonsense to have people stop looking into it.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Explicit warnings not to look into it are up front, early on in the article. The warnings seem to have shaky reasoning to begin with.
